quotes.note: The authorized opening restores the clipped context: this is external description of Ericson within sustained third-person narration.
Base narration refers to Ericson as “He” while presenting his inward attitude toward the sea from an external narrating position.
Authorial commentary about the Atlantic contains no character-narrator or otherwise decisive person marker.
The gnomic “You” means people generally and is not sustained story-specific second-person narration.
Extended panoramic base narration observes waves, ships, and endangered men from a nonparticipating external position.
Panoramic historical narration surveys nations and the Atlantic campaign from outside the represented action.
The severe mid-sentence clipping leaves neither boundaries nor enough local narration to determine person.

person_note: The controlling voice is a nonparticipating omniscient third-person narrator. The authorized opening and several Goodreads event passages independently show external narration with access to characters and broad historical or panoramic commentary, while the Gale structural account explicitly identifies the narrator as third person across the seven-part novel. Shifts among Ericson, Lockhart, Ferraby, other crewmen, and families ashore are changes in focalization, not person alternation. The universal “you” in q00784 is gnomic rather than second person, and no researched source indicated a first-person frame, epistolary structure, or sustained alternate-person section.
